claim.quote: We report a measurement of the positive muon lifetime to a precision of 1.0 parts per million (ppm); it is the most precise particle lifetime ever measured.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal version is Phys. Rev. Lett. 106, 041803 (2011).

key_value_text.quote: The combined results give tau_{mu^+}(MuLan) = 2196980.3(2.2) ps, more than 15 times as precise as any previous experiment.

name: Measurement of the Positive Muon Lifetime and Determination of the Fermi Constant to Part-per-Million Precision

significance.quote: The muon lifetime gives the most precise value for the Fermi constant: G_F(MuLan) = 1.1663788 (7) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.6 ppm).
significance.value: Lifetime to 1.0 ppm; Fermi constant G_F(MuLan) = 1.1663788(7) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.6 ppm)

summary.plain: MuLan timed more than two trillion muon decays and measured the muon lifetime to one part in a million, the most precise lifetime ever measured for a particle. From it the strength of the weak force, the Fermi constant, follows to 0.6 parts per million.
summary.technical: Positive muon lifetime tau = 2196980.3(2.2) ps from more than 2 x 10^12 decays with two stopping-target configurations, more than 15 times more precise than any previous experiment; G_F(MuLan) = 1.1663788(7) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.6 ppm); also used to extract the mu-p singlet capture rate and the induced pseudoscalar coupling g_P.

title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Lifetime and Determination of the Fermi Constant to Part-per-Million Precision
why_it_matters: The abstract says the muon lifetime gives the most precise value for the Fermi constant.
